about: The Baptist's sentence at the Jordan, with one word altered. John says Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccátum mundi — the sin of the world, in the singular; the Mass says peccáta, the sins. The people then say the centurion's line three times, exactly as the priest said it a moment ago over himself, and receive with the form he used, changed in one word: ánimam tuam for ánimam meam. He begins at the Epistle side, and says the whole sentence to each communicant while signing the ciborium with the Host.

s01.narrative: Genuflecting, the priest takes the ciborium in his left hand and a single particle in his right, holds it a little above the ciborium, turns to those about to communicate, and says:

s02.translation: Behold the Lamb of God, behold Him who takes away the sins of the world.

s03.narrative: Then he says, and the people say with him:

s04.translation: Lord, I am not worthy that Thou shouldst enter under my roof, but only say the word, and my soul shall be healed.

s05.translation: Lord, I am not worthy that Thou shouldst enter under my roof, but only say the word, and my soul shall be healed.

s06.translation: Lord, I am not worthy that Thou shouldst enter under my roof, but only say the word, and my soul shall be healed.

s07.narrative: The words said three times over, he goes to their right, that is, to the Epistle side, and gives the Sacrament to each, making the sign of the cross with it over the ciborium and saying:

s08.translation: May the Body of our Lord Jesus Christ keep thy soul unto life everlasting. Amen.

s09.narrative: All having communicated, he returns to the altar saying nothing, and gives them no blessing, since he will give it at the end of Mass.

w001.function: An interjection, and old enough that Latin no longer felt the pointing finger in it. It takes the nominative, not the accusative an English verb would want.

w004.function: Repeated, and the second time it points not at a title but at a deed: behold the one who takes away.

w006.function: Third person: the priest speaks about Him, holding Him up. In the Agnus Dei a few minutes earlier the same clause was second person, tollis, because there He was addressed.

w007.function: The Gospel at the Jordan has peccátum, the sin of the world in the singular; the Mass says the sins.

w009.function: The centurion's sentence again, this time in the mouth of those about to receive; the priest said the same words over himself a moment ago.

w012.function: The people strike the breast on this word, as the priest did on his.

w067.function: The one word that separates this form from the one the priest says over himself, which has meam. Everything else in the sentence is identical.
